Year blank; en.wikipedia dates it 1812, de.wikipedia 'ed. um 1812'. Three movements, 30:19 and 30:30 on the two CDs
Year blank; de.wikipedia lists the C-major trio Op. 4 as 'ed. um 1799'. Three movements, 20 min on both CDs
Rahter 1911 print holds Nos. 5-8; Rawlins Trio (Albany) plays those four, 7.8 min in all

Mosaiques recording 20.6 min; c. 1802 is IMSLP's guess for the undated Breitkopf print

Title page of the Breitkopf print reads 'avec Flute ou Violon', flute first, and the only recording found (Euridice, 25.4 min) uses flute. Entry makes violin the main part and flute the alternative, which is the reverse; with flute first the work would have no string part. No recording with violin found. Owner to decide scope and order
Recordings run 32:46 (MDG) and 39:27 (Brilliant), IMSLP 40; 36 is a fair mean. No. 2 (Op. 7) runs about 26 min

Three movements, 21.9 (CPO) and 21.2 min (Brilliant); 1894

fixes.notes: Manuscript has four movements, the first two reused from the B minor Trio; the recording plays only the new III-IV

results.note: IMSLP: four movements, I-II are the B minor Trio's movements transposed, III-IV are new. Brilliant records only III (Scherzo) and IV (Adagio molto-Presto), 8.4 min. Notes corrected; entry kept because the recording is of this trio
Three movements, 15.9 and 17.8 min; 1945 on the manuscript. IMSLP gives a 1994 'first publication' but Brilliant calls it unpublished
Wikipedia: Op. 24 (1942) for 2 violins, 2 violas, cello; four movements, 27:49 (Brilliant) and 27:17 (MDG)
cpo: 14:19, three movements, Adagio 'Le lacrime di Petrarca'; autographs of Op. 3 dated 1785

results.note: Wikipedia lists a 'Quartet in G minor (fragment; c. 1916/17)'; the Bridge Quartet record it as Quartet-Movement in G minor, 7:44. Kept as an unfinished single movement performed as it stands (Bridge Quartet CD and a Wigmore Hall centenary concert programme); year added, notes say 'unfinished' per the curation brief
de.wikipedia: Op. 65 Klaviertrio e-Moll, Simrock, Berlin, 1927 (publication; composition date not found). Four movements 28:54 on the cpo disc

Stamic Quartet: Allegro vivace, Poco adagio, Allegro di molto, 23.9 min; D minor is No. 6. Same set as Op. 26 (Andre, Aug 1793), so the aka is right; c. 1790 is IMSLP's date for the Sieber print and may be a little early

Andre published Op. 23 in June 1793; the set was written for the cello-playing Frederick William II (the 'Prussian' quartets), four movements in C major. No commercial recording found; free modern score (Bernhardsson/Ackerman) plus a Kammerphilharmonie Bremen programme listing it (Friday 17 May, year not shown) pass the floor. Minutes unknown

IMSLP's 1790 is its date for an undated Sieber print; Gombart (Augsburg) issued the set in 1798 per the Rheinfurth list on wranitzky.com, so 'c. 1798' stands. cpo (Almaviva Quartett): Allegro 11.3, Adagio 8.1, Rondo 5.3 = 24.7 min

Andre issued Op. 29 on 6 Oct 1794 (keys F, C, A), two violins, two violas, cello. Festival page: first known modern performance of the first quintet, Stamic Quartet with K. Plocek, 2008. Minutes unknown

Brilliant: four movements incl. Menuetto grazioso, 19.8 min. Andre's catalogue dates Op. 17 Livre 1 (B-flat, E-flat, C) to 16 March 1792, so 'c. 1790' is a little early; left as it may be a composition date
Brilliant titles it Op. 3 No. 3: Allegro moderato, Adagio, Menuetto, Finale, 19.0 min. Andre Op. 20 (15 Feb 1793) has F, C, G, hence the other numberings in aka
Andre Op. 32 Livre 1 (G), 20 May 1799; Prague Trio: Allegro brillante, Andante, Rondo, 15.5 min

The Hoffmeister print is for flute, oboe, violin, two violas and cello. The only violin-for-viola source found is a 2025 IMSLP arrangement of No. IV by T. Bolzonella, or the Stamic Quartet's own seating; neither is a composer or first-edition alternative. Entry otherwise right (E-flat is No. 3, 14.6 min)
Supraphon: C major, four movements as in notes, 20.3 min

note: Fixes: Wilms Op. 30 and Op. 4 and Woyrsch Op. 65 gained years (publication dates from Wikipedia); Wranitzky Sextet No. 3 lost an unsanctioned viola-for-violin alternative; Wuorinen Divertimento is a single movement of about 11 min (form short); Wolf-Ferrari C minor trio notes and Wood G minor movement year/notes corrected. Doubts: Woelfl Op. 42 (flute named first and the only recording is with flute, so the string part is the alternative) and Wolfe Big Beautiful Dark and Scary (15 min per composer, 8:44 on the recording). IMSLP mismatches for Williams No. 6 and Wranitzky Op. 32 No. 4 were IMSLP errors. Wranitzky Op. 17 No. 2 and Op. 16 No. 6 dates (c. 1790) may be a little early (Andre printed Op. 17 in 1792); left.
